release: Makes the SEO report readable, and stops it lying in two directions. (1) The report body rendered as raw JSON text and fragments of the audited site's own DOM: the SEO tool embedded every audited page's full HTML in the report's data island, and the first </script> in that HTML closed the tag — so the issue list was empty too. The payload is now escaped so no page content can break it, and the SEO report no longer carries page source at all (measured on sgen.com: 31.6 MB of HTML, previously written twice per run). (2) The graded summary printed NOT RUN for every check that PASSED — 8 of them on sgen.com, including canonical and indexability — because a passing row carried no identity. Every check now names itself, so clean reads as clean. New: the SEO report has a Content & readability section (thin content and readability, plus Copy Review flags for assistant boilerplate, unfilled placeholders, AI-tell phrasing and paragraph rhythm). Also carries the 4.10.x SEO false-positive fixes: redirects and 404s are no longer audited as pages (26 bogus 'Missing title' and 1 bogus NOINDEX on sgen.com), robots.txt is parsed by User-agent group so an AI-training opt-out is not a CRITICAL, and an SEO-only run no longer signs itself '0/92 pages rendered'. The SEO tool's configuration also moves where the rest of the app keeps it: the 17 check toggles and the page ceiling are now in the Settings gear (with Include all / Exclude all and a live 'scoring on N / 17' count), and the panel keeps only what is per-run — the URL and the scope. The ceiling previously existed in two places at once. Duplicate titles/descriptions are shown disabled with the reason on a This-page run instead of being silently unticked, which also stops a switch back to Whole site from re-ticking a check you deliberately turned off. No scoring change: no rule was added, removed or rescored, and the new Copy Review rows carry weight 0 and status manual — so a score from 4.11.0 is directly comparable to one from 4.10.0.
